title: HYDRON EVO: MULTI TBPS SPACE BACKBONE NETWORK (ARTES 4.0 SL SPL 3A.241) EXPRO+
description: Objective:The objective of this study is to investigate the High-throughput Optical Network evolution (HydRON EVO) as the backbonenetwork enabling a total capacity of tens to hundreds TbpsTargeted Improvements:To assess the feasibility of optical space backbone network with total capacity in the range of tens to hundreds TbpsDescription:Following the terrestrial network analogy, backbone (long-haul) networks provide capacity beyond Terabit-per-second (Tbps) per single line (with links beyond 800 Gbps per wavelength). The current HydRON (High-throughput Optical Network) demonstration system will demonstrate single-link communications from 2.5G to 100Gbps, addressing both user access and the lower datarate backbone links. To enable growth of optical space networks, as an extension of the terrestrial fibre network, a space backbone is required to support multi-Tbps capacity in space. The backbone should be interoperable and interface with multiple networks like the one developed in HydRON demonstration system. However, using DWDM technologies and commercial coherent transceivers, the single link capacity can be increased beyond Tbps, and by aggregating multiple channels the network capacity can be increased to tens or even hundreds Tbps.This activity shall address the design and technology trade-offs of a space network backbone exceeding several Tbps and serving other space networks. It shall provide a set of requirements and a system concept. It shall be verified by analysis that the system concept is scalable at higher rates. Interoperability aspects shall be analysed, to guarantee the connectivity among networks (including terrestrial fibre networks). Technology gaps shall be identified and technology roadmap provided. Finally, the activity shall propose a demonstrator concept where the relevant technologyas well as the operational concept can be demonstrated, to further push the technology borders in terms of data rates/capacity aiming to maintain the strategic leadership position of the Europen/Canadian Industry The activity will also contribute to the evolutionof ESTOL.

title: 3U VERSION OF THE ADVANCED POWER ARCHITECTURE (APA) - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop a small three-rack-unit version of the Advanced Power Architecture (APA) with aim of having a highly compact architecture fit for small missions.Description: The Advanced Power Architecture (APA) is being designed for general ESA mission /medium scale platform but is not addressing smaller mission needs. This activity aims at developing the APA concept in a three-rack-unit (3U) version; this footprint would be suitable for smaller satellites up to 500 kg. The activity targets to investigate the miniaturisation of the already identified functions by integrating novel technologies such as digital control and Gallium Nitride High-Electron Mobility transistor (GaN HEM FET). The Advanced Data Handling Architecture (ADHA) has already a 3U version which, if coupled with a 3U version of the APA, it would enable a single frame for a very compact avionics system. In fact, the APA will provide the input power interface, the TM/TC interface, the internal power rails and the internal communication bus. Thus, any platform function not needing internal high speed data communication buses could fit perfectly in the 3U APA. For instance, the solar array drive function or any motor drive function, propulsion valves drive functions, thermal control, etc. The activity targets to enhance industrialisation of power units for mid-size satellites by having the full power system functionality integrated in one unit. If deemed adequate for the application, a cost-effective solution could be available by having the components as COTS. A strong focus on manufacturability and industrialisation will be done, focusing on automatic manufacturing, planar transformers, SMD components, etc. This activity focuses on the development of the Solar Array Regulator (SAR) module with miniaturised DC/DC converter and on the Solar Array Drive Electronics (SADE) demonstrating the applicability of the concept to the entire avionics functions. These will be the firstbuilding blocks for the development of the complete functionality. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Converter andfilter size reduction thanks to the use of HEM FET (GaN) - Inclusion of the Solar Array Drive Electronics to embed all potential EPS need - Design and manufacturing of a breadboard - Test of the breadboard - Validation and verification - Way forward for industrialization

title: SUSTAINABLE MINERAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT - EXPRO+
description: Sustainable mineral resource management involves the responsible extraction, use, and conservation of mineral resources to meet present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs. It emphasizes efficient mining practices, minimizing environmental impacts, and restoring ecosystems after extraction. An important component of this approach is the use of Earth observation technologies, which allow the detection of (critical earth) minerals, continuous monitoring of mining activities, land degradation and water quality. The development of novel EO solutions and tools improve transparency, support better decision-making, andhelp detect unsustainable practices in near real time. Combined with recycling, resource efficiency, and strong environmental policies, Earth observation enhances the ability to balance economic development with environmental protection and social responsibility,ensuring long-term sustainability of mineral resources.

title: KA-BAND HIGH POWER ACTIVE TRANSMIT INTEGRATED ANTENNA FOR LEO SATCOM APPLICATIONS (ARTES AT 5B.257) (ON DELEGATION REQUEST)
description: Objective:The objective of this activity is to design, develop and test a scaled engineering model of a Ka-Band 45dBW EIRP class active transmit highly integrated antenna for LEO constellations (orbits up to about 1000km) for governmental and commercial application. This includes a thermal management system compatible with high power requirements, use of SiPs to reduce the volume and higher number of elements and beams.Targeted Improvements:-Enabling 45dBW EIRP class active phased array antenna for governmental and commercial connectivity applications.-2 to 3 times increased number of beams compared to state of the art today in Europe.-40 to 50%improvement in mass compared to analogue beamforming-based architecture.Description:Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations require high-capacity integrated active phased array antennas. Today the active antennas available can guarantee only limited flexibility in terms of number of beams, bandwidth and power dissipation. For both commercial and government applications, there is a demand for active antennas composed of more than 1000 radiating elements and enabling a minimum of 40 to 64 simultaneous beams. However, the high integration requirements for accommodating in LEO satellites operating in orbits up to about 1000km creates thermal management challenges. In order to achieve these challenging requirements, current active antenna technology must be significantly improved. On the thermal management, novel heat dissipation concepts must be investigated, developed and demonstrated. Exploring new promising solutions including Pulsed Heat Pipes should be considered. On the beamforming network, trade-off between fully digital and hybrid should be performed, considering the latest technology available on digital processors (using ultra-deep sub-micron technologies) and System-in-Package (SiP) commercial solutions. On radiating elements, recent promising results have been achieved on antenna based on waveguide and PCB technology.This activity will study, develop, and implement a beamforming architecture and thermal management solution for LEO high-capacity integrated active phased array antennas. The selected concept will be implemented as a scaled engineering model and tested in critical environment.This activity will be implemented in a phased approach where:-Phase 1 will study design concepts of beamforming architectures and thermal management solutions for active antenna technology. The solution will be designed and optimised, considering aspects such as the beam forming network architecture, the digital signal processing architecture, the amplification sizing and the thermal management. This phase will include de-risking module implementation at breadboard level with testing. The budget for Phase 1 is up to 900 kEuro.-In the second Phase, a scaled engineering model shall be produced, capable of operating over the full bandwidth to produce flexible number of beams between 4 to 10. The design must be scalable and must include active elements and optimised thermal management system. This scaled engineering model will be developed and validated in a critical environment. The scaled engineering model shall comprise one or more representative payload building blocks, including frequency conversion, signal processing beam forming, high power amplification, filtering and radiating element functions.
